title: Normalized finite-projective constant models under ordinary derived pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the constant ring sheaves $C_{n,T}=(R/t^n)_T$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}C_{n,T}$ with projections $\pi_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For a scheme morphism $g:T\to W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $g^{-1}$ and $c^g_{R/t^n}$ be the inverse image and constant-section maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Give it the structural ring map $c_g:g^{-1}B_W\to B_T$ characterized by $\pi_{T,n}c_g=c^g_{R/t^n}g^{-1}(\pi_{W,n})$. Write $g_B^*M=B_T\otimes_{g^{-1}B_W}g^{-1}M$ for ordinary module pullback, and $P_g=Lg_B^*$ with computation counit $\epsilon_Q:P_g[Q]\to[g_B^*Q]$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $[Q]$ denotes localization, and tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $v:V\to U$ be any scheme morphism and let $L^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules, zero outside some finite integer interval, with each $L^q$ a direct summand of a finite free $R$-module. Put $M_T^\bullet=B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{L^\bullet}_T$ for $T=U,V$, where underlining means termwise constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and the map $\underline R_T\to B_T$ has $n$-th projection the constant quotient $R\to R/t^n$.

There is a natural isomorphism of complexes
$$\gamma_L:v_B^*M_U^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}M_V^\bullet.$$
For $L^q=R^r$ with standard basis $e_j$, its degree-$q$ map and inverse have the formulas
$$b\otimes(ae_j)\longmapsto b\,c_v(a)e_j,\qquad be_j\longmapsto b\otimes e_j,$$
where $a$ is a local section of $v^{-1}B_U$ and $b$ a local section of $B_V$. For each specified splitting $L^q\xrightarrow{\iota_q}R^{r_q}\xrightarrow{p_q}L^q$ with $p_q\iota_q=1$, $\gamma_L^q$ is the restriction of this finite-free isomorphism to the image of the same scalar idempotent $e_q=\iota_qp_q\in M_{r_q}(R)$. It is independent of the splitting and natural in every $R$-linear map between finite projective modules, hence commutes with the specified differentials of $L^\bullet$.

Every term of $M_U^\bullet$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $M_U^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The specified ordinary computation counit is an isomorphism, and in the derived category the normalized model comparison is the isomorphism
$$P_v[M_U^\bullet]\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{M_U}}[v_B^*M_U^\bullet]\xrightarrow{[\gamma_L]}[M_V^\bullet].$$
No flatness of $B_U$ over $R$ or of $c_v$, and no completion of this comparison, is required.

proof.text: Prove the direct-image scalar square by projecting to every finite coefficient quotient and applying naturality of constant-section maps [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction]. Evaluate this square on constant R-sections; the two scalar restrictions of the module pushforward agree.

proof.text: Construct explicitly the adjunction between constant modules and evaluation at a terminal object, using constant-module sheafification, and the adjunction between the independent-universe scalar-extension functor and restriction of scalars [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Their composite identifies maps from the model with R-linear maps into terminal sections. Step 1 identifies the right adjoints before and after ordinary pushforward. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives a natural isomorphism for every R-module, hence for finite projectives. Evaluate the hom-equivalence identity on x to obtain the normalized formula at the terminal object, and use restriction naturality to obtain it on every object. Injectivity of the two adjunction hom-equivalences proves uniqueness.

proof.text: Linearity and the adjunction unit give the two finite-free basis formulas. Naturality gives the displayed retract equations for any specified splitting, independently of the splitting. Apply naturality to each differential to obtain the complex isomorphism. These are direct categorical calculations.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; specialization to the published ordinary completed-integral module pullback, and uniqueness of total left derived functors.

proof.text: The scalar realization of R is the unit module by the proved constant-unit and scalar-extension-unit isomorphisms [lem-sfb-scalar-perfect-chart-finite-free]. Being a left adjoint, the model preserves finite products. Thus it sends R^n to the finite free sheaf. A finite projective module is a retract of R^n by Mathlib; its realization is the corresponding retract. The finite-free retract flatness lemma [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model] proves flatness of each term. The bounded interval gives boundedness above, so [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] proves K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; specialization to the published ordinary completed-integral module pullback, and uniqueness of total left derived functors.

proof.text: Use the existing canonical computation theorem [lem-tw-ordinary-integral-good-complex-counit] and naturality of its complex comparison to show ordinary pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes. Every complex has a resolution in this class [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The resolving-class theorem [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] therefore constructs a derived pair computing on this class in any specified derived-category universe. Uniqueness of total left derived functors transfers invertibility to the arbitrary LF and epsilon in the statement. Apply this to the bounded flat model complex of step 4. Finally localization sends the complex comparison to an isomorphism, and composition with the computation counit is invertible.
